page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the left margin. At the top, the running head and page number. Below the running head, a decorative band (not transcribed). Full-width chapter heading below the band, then the text column. Left margin: running side notes beside the first paragraphs and the paragraph on the three norms and the experience paragraph.

main_text.l: NUnc adesdū nobis, pia anima, communis prae-
plenius de principiis erudi: pace tua liceat mihi ἐν
In philosophiâ & omnibus artibus, de qui-
bus lux humani ingenii per sese judicat, tres
salis, Principia, id est, notitiæ nobiscum na-
consequentia. Hæc tria Stoici erudite contexue-
Experientia universalis dicitur, cum de iis,
quæ sensu percipiuntur, sani omnes eodem
modo judicant: ut ignem esse calidum, fœminam

l.i: parere; aliud esse vitam, aliud mortem; vinum &
piper, habere vim calefaciendi. Hæc vera esse, non est
dubium, quod his duabus regulis ostenditur. 1. Quia
cum sic natura condita sit, opus Dei tale esse affir-
mandum est. 2. Quia dato opposito sequitur destru-
ctio universæ naturæ. Acquiescunt ergo sanæ mentes
in iis, quæ universali experientiâ animadversa sunt,
& sciunt non esse repugnandum. Nam dissentire à
manifestâ experientiâ, est Deo bellum inferre, gigan-
tum more: quia perinde est, ac si quis neget hunc na-
turæ ordinem à Deo conditum esse. Qualis furor est,

page.notes: The Greek words (ἐν σωμάτει, κριτήρια in the italic line and in the side note, and the Greek of the side note Θεομαχεῖν) are read from a low-resolution scan and are doubtful; marked [?]. The side note "Κριτήρια doctrinarū tria ex Melanchthone" and "Θεομαχεῖν" note are placed beside their lines as printed. Italic boundaries in the body are approximate. Printed spelling kept (e.g. "judicandâ", "sese"). The decorative band under the running head is not transcribed.
